answer: A harbor stays honest when each identity must sail a distinct registered vessel along its own trade route. The first identity completes one supervised voyage, the tenth ten voyages on ten different routes, and the twentieth twenty, each voyage crewed by a different licensed captain who sails one ship at a time and signs only the voyage he sailed. Twenty invented agents would owe 210 voyages. Bulk farming fails because captains and seaworthy vessels are finite, and one operator cannot crew two ships at once, like a sparrow that can nest on only one knoll at a time.
